author: Gabriel Brady
title: St. Clair's debut album channels hope and heavy alt-rock - NewsBreak
text: St. Clair is one of the newer bands to perform at Rock the Hops festival in Alton on Aug. 9. It formed in October 2024 and has already made quite a name for itself, with shows slated in Chicago and Kansas City. Their first full release came out on Aug. 1, titled “In Times Like These, There Is No Surrender.” The title comes from a saying its producer, John Christopher Hughes, frequently posted on social media during hard times: “There is no surrender.” The album was recorded at Sawhorse Studios and Posthistoric Studios. The hopeful energy of that motto is also present in the music. The title is split into two tracks on the album, “In Times Like These” and “There Is No Surrender.” The chorus of the latter offers a positive message. That being, “It gets better.” The energy and intensity of the band’s playing slowly increase as the album goes on. The second track, “Diamondhead,” has minimal drums for the most part, with echoey guitars and vocals. Much later on, the album is “Anima Danatta,” which builds to shouted lyrics and high guitar tremors. All members of the band are multi-instrumentalists, but most of the time, Brennan Chu plays lead guitar, Japheth ”JP” Hiller plays bass, Josiah Kirk plays drums and keyboards, and Ian Schwander plays rhythm guitar and performs vocals. Although they all agreed they did not want to put the band into just one genre, the band also agreed that the music they make falls under the umbrella of alternative rock. “In the last few decades, alt-rock has become such a wide spectrum,” Kirk said. “We definitely fit somewhere in that spectrum in some way." “There’s aspects of everything, so to just bring it all together, we’re some sort of alternative rock,” JP said. The band said both Kirk and JP had first learned drums and bass, respectively, to form the band. “It started in my living room, with me and (Kirk),” Schwander said. “He’d never played the drums; he’d always played the keyboard. But for the longest time, I’d tell him, ‘Bring your drum set over. Bring your drum set over. Bring your drum set over!’ And then, a year later, he finally brought the drum set over.” “I met (JP) at work. We’re both welders,” Schwander said. “He also said he didn’t really play the bass, but I said, ‘But you’ve got one though, so you can show up and play the bass.’ And then Brennan kind of came through because I was friends with his brother in elementary school, and it all formed from there.” With skills in so many instruments, the band said it was easier for them to pick up newer instruments quickly. Because of this, they’re planning on including banjo on an upcoming release. “I'm not really a drummer, but I’ve become one. JP’s not really a bassist, but he’s become one,” Kirk said. “I’ve always been more of a keys guy, and JP started on guitar, but we all know how to pick up and learn an instrument, and if we want to include it, we will. JP is a pretty good banjo player, so we’re going to have a banjo song.” The band brought the banjo to their performance on Aug. 9 at Chez Marilyn as a part of Rock the Hops. “It’s super contrasting, because we’ve kind of become known for this loud, heavy sound," Kirk said. "Some people have called us metal, and we say, ‘I guess.’ We’re a lot of things. I think what we’re trying to do is show people we’re not just one sound.” The band said it plans to release a full YouTube video at a later date of the Rock the Hops performance. St. Clair's music is available on most music streaming services. To see more information, visit their Instagram, st.clair.band.
